ratings_why.fun: Over a 7 because Bloom turns the copy rule upside down: the same Ivy Shoot, Egg or Mistletoe-drained husk is a dead host in one build and the perfect root in another, so every turn asks you to re-plan the tree.
ratings_why.distinct: Trees of hosts layered on top of the slot grid, and climbing the enemy, feel new; underneath, the copy-half rule is a familiar stat-sharing multiplier.

verdict_why: Nothing is broken or unreadable now; further passes would change the tribe's flavour rather than improve it.

points.text: Unlisted combo: Woodbine, Barley-sugar Twiner and Kissing Bough climb the host they buff, so each copies half its own buff back. Worth a line in the Johnny tricks so players find it.
Mistletoe Clump climbing Dodder Thread copies the steal, then drains Dodder next turn: a cross-card loop that is fun and finite. Consider naming Dodder Thread as a good Clump host.

Golden Lady Hedera's 'twice' brings back the doubling-per-level case removed from golden Lattice Ivy (two golden Hederas stacked give 4x). Rare enough to keep as a high roll; say so in the tier check.
Hanger-on is the only plain card in a tribe of tricks. It could pay for an enemy host too (a Dodder that is climbing), tying the economy to the gatecrasher line.
Old Man's Beard plus Cousin Dodder is the best combo in the set: each kill re-climbs the biggest enemy and feeds a third of the dead one. Keep it hot; the owner can cap it later.

standouts.why: A climber that is also a host for stolen stats, and that climbs back: three jobs from one card.
A junction that rewires the tree's geometry, so where you put it is a real puzzle.
Moves stats instead of adding them, which makes a Bloom root out of any unit and a sell-husk out of a dying one.

weakest.why: Gold for a condition that is almost always met; no decision.
A plain Start of Combat buff; only its self-echo makes it interesting.
A vanilla buff-on-play; fine filler at Tier 1, nothing to discover.

flags.note: Golden copies stacked on each other double per level of chain.
With Cousin Dodder chaining kills, a third of each dead enemy can swing a fight hard.
Pays the root per climber, then the whole chain copies it; a deep Grand Oak can grow fast.
